mainTopic: Splitting one document into a part that works and a part that fails (רב נחמן and רב אשי); who contests a גט; a שליח who cannot say בפני נכתב; and how גיטי נשים and שחרורי עבדים are alike.
overview: The עמוד opens at the end of רבי שמעון's view that a slave given 'all the property' goes free, which was brought to show that one document can work for one part and fail for another. The גמרא pushes back: רב נחמן ruled like רבי מאיר, not רבי שמעון. But רב נחמן also ruled that a שכיב מרע who wrote all his property to his slave and recovered takes back the property while the slave stays free, which looks like splitting a statement. רב אשי explains that רב נחמן followed רבי מאיר for a different reason: a release document must fully cut off the slave, and holding back property means it does not. Next, the גמרא asks who the 'contesters' of a גט are in the משנה. One person is not enough and two would create a tie, so it must be the husband himself. A new משנה teaches that if the שליח bringing a גט from overseas cannot say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם, the גט is confirmed through its signing witnesses. רב יוסף explains that the שליח was capable when he delivered it and became a חרש afterward. Finally, a ברייתא begins listing three ways גיטי נשים and שחרורי עבדים are alike, and the third way continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the slave always goes free
steps.stepSummary: The end of a quoted משנה: according to רבי שמעון, a slave given 'all the property' always goes free. The only exception is when the master clearly held back a tiny fraction.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is always a free man, unless the master says: 'All my property is given to so-and-so my slave, except for one ten-thousandth of it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote of רבי שמעון's opinion. It is bringing this as support for the idea that one document can work for part of what it says and not for the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the master kept some land, so the gift of 'all the property' is not fully true, רבי שמעון still says the slave goes free. So the freeing works even though the property part does not. The only case where the slave stays a slave is when the master explicitly held back 'one ten-thousandth', because the slave himself might be part of that held-back portion.

keyTerms.meaning: A free man (a slave who has been set free)
My property
Ten thousand
So-and-so

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of a new topic. It is the tail end of a quoted source that the גמרא is using as proof for an argument that started before this section.

phrases.english: He is always a free man,
phrases.notes: These are רבי שמעון's words, the end of a משנה about a master who wrote his property over to his slave.

phrases.english: unless he says: "All my property is given
to so-and-so my slave
except for one ten-thousandth of it."

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם הוּא בֶּן חוֹרִין, עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted source that is being brought as proof that we split a statement.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that one document can work for part of what it says (freeing the slave) and fail for another part (the property).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's opinion in the משנה about writing property to a slave.

steps.title: But the הלכה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof. רב נחמן ruled that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר, even though רבי יוסי praised רבי שמעון's view with a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב יוסף בר מניומי say in the name of רב נחמן: even though רבי יוסי praised רבי שמעון, the הלכה follows רבי מאיר? As it was taught: when these words were said before רבי יוסי, he read this פסוק about him: 'He kisses the lips of one who gives a right answer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from רבי שמעון. The proof does not help, because the practical ruling does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says that if the master kept any land at all, the slave does not go free. So רבי מאיר does not split the document. Since רב נחמן rules like רבי מאיר, רבי שמעון's view cannot be our basis for splitting a statement. The ברייתא about רבי יוסי's praise shows how strong רבי שמעון's view seemed, yet it was still not accepted as הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Praised
The practical ruling follows (so-and-so)
Right, correct, straightforward

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי's praise does not decide the הלכה. Even a view that earned a 'kiss' of approval can be outweighed. Here the ruling goes like רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yosef bar Minyumi say
that Rav Naḥman said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקִּילֵּס רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֶת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן –
phrases.english: Even though Rabbi Yosei praised Rabbi Shimon,
the halakha follows Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר holds the other view in that משנה: if the master kept any land, the slave does not go free.

phrases.english: as it was taught:
When these words were said before Rabbi Yosei,
he recited this verse about him:
"He kisses the lips of one who gives a right answer"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof brought in step 1 by showing that the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from רבי שמעון that we split a statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A proof from a rejected opinion cannot establish the הלכה. רב נחמן rules like רבי מאיר, who does not free the slave when the master kept something back.

steps.title: Does רב נחמן really reject splitting?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רב נחמן really holds this way. It quotes another ruling of his: a שכיב מרע who wrote all his property to his slave and then recovered can take back the property but not the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב נחמן really say this? But didn't רב יוסף בר מניומי say in the name of רב נחמן: a שכיב מרע who wrote all his property to his slave, and then recovered, can take back the property but cannot take back the slave?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns around and attacks the challenge from step 2. It shows that רב נחמן himself seems to split a statement in another case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the שכיב מרע case, one document gave both the property and the slave's freedom. After the man recovers, the property part is cancelled, but the freedom part stays in force. That is splitting a statement, which seems to clash with רב נחמן siding against רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Did (so-and-so) really say this? (signals a contradiction)
A person on his deathbed, seriously ill
And he got up (recovered from the illness)
Can take back, retract

steps.whyThisMatters: This case becomes the key test of whether רב נחמן accepts splitting a statement (פלגינן דיבורא).

phrases.english: And did Rav Naḥman really say this?
phrases.notes: "This" means the idea that we don't split one document into a part that works and a part that doesn't.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yosef bar Minyumi say that Rav Naḥman said:
A person on his deathbed who wrote
all his property to his slave,
and he recovered,
can take back the property,
but cannot take back the slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 2 that רב נחמן does not accept splitting a statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רב נחמן rejects splitting a statement because he rules like רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן's own ruling in the שכיב מרע case keeps the slave's freedom while cancelling the property gift. That is exactly splitting a statement.

steps.title: Why the property returns but the slave stays free
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the two halves of רב נחמן's ruling. The property goes back because it was a deathbed gift. The slave stays free because he is already known publicly as a free man.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can take back the property, because it is a deathbed gift. He cannot take back the slave, because the slave already has the reputation of a free man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains each half of רב נחמן's ruling. This sharpens the point that the same document is being treated in two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deathbed gift is given on the assumption that the giver will die, so it falls away if he recovers. The slave's freedom stays in force, because once people know him as free, his status is not reversed. One document is now valid for one part and void for the other, which shows that רב נחמן does split a statement.

keyTerms.meaning: A deathbed gift (cancelled if the giver recovers)
A name (reputation) has gone out about him

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן rules that the property goes back but the slave stays free. That looks like splitting a statement, which clashes with his ruling like רבי מאיר against רבי שמעון.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the master never really freed the slave. It is saying the freedom holds even though the property part of the same document falls away.

phrases.english: He can take back the property:
it is a deathbed gift,
and he cannot take back the slave:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי יָצָא עָלָיו שֵׁם בֶּן חוֹרִין!
phrases.english: because the name 'free man' has already gone out about him!
phrases.notes: Literally "a name went out on him": people already know him as a free man.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹזֵר בַּנְּכָסִים – מַתְּנַת שְׁכִיב מְרַע הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the two halves of רב נחמן's ruling to explain each one, which completes the challenge from step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That רב נחמן does split a statement (פלגינן דיבורא).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's ruling about a שכיב מרע who wrote all his property to his slave and then recovered.

steps.title: רב אשי: the real reason is that the document doesn't fully cut the slave off
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that רב נחמן followed רבי מאיר for a different reason: a document that holds back some property is not a fully 'cutting' document.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: There, the reason is that it is not a document that fully cuts off the connection.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge against רב נחמן. It gives a new reason why he ruled like רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We had thought רב נחמן followed רבי מאיר because he holds you cannot split one statement in two. רב אשי says no: a שטר שחרור must fully cut the slave off from his master, like a גט. When the master holds back some property, the slave might be part of what was held back, so the document is not fully cutting.

keyTerms.meaning: Cutting off / severing; a document that fully ends the connection
A document of release (here, the slave's שטר שחרור)
This is the reason

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's ruling like רבי מאיר is not about splitting a statement. It is about the rule that a release document must fully cut off the bond.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
There, this is the reason:
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case where רב נחמן ruled like רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: because it is not a fully cutting document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the tension raised in steps 2-4 by giving a new reason for רב נחמן's ruling
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-explaining the reason behind a ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן ruled like רבי מאיר because he holds we do not split a statement
steps.terutzMaskana: He ruled like רבי מאיר because a document that holds back property is not כרות; on splitting statements he can agree we do split

steps.title: How many people must contest a גט?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about contested גיטין and asks how many contesters are meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If there are people contesting it, it should be ratified through its signers.' How many make a contestation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה and asks a question about it, setting up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a גט brought within ארץ ישראל usually needs no declaration. But if someone contests it, it needs ratification through its signers. The גמרא wants to know who counts as a contester: one person or two?

keyTerms.meaning: People who contest (object to) a document, claiming it is forged
A contestation / objection against a document
It should be ratified through its signers (by confirming the signatures)

phrases.english: If there are those who contest it,
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה about a גט brought from one place in ארץ ישראל to another.

phrases.english: it should be ratified through its signers.
A contestation: how many people?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם יֵשׁ עָלָיו עוֹרְרִין, יִתְקַיֵּים בְּחוֹתְמָיו: עַרְעָר כַּמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How many people make up an עַרְעָר that forces the גט to be ratified

steps.title: One contester can't be enough
steps.stepSummary: If one person contesting were enough, that goes against רבי יוחנן, who says a contestation needs at least two people.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say one contester, didn't רבי יוחנן say: everyone agrees a contestation is no fewer than two people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first option, one contester, and rejects it using a rule of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single witness cannot take down a document. So by רבי יוחנן's rule, one person saying 'it's forged' is not a real עַרְעָר at all, and the משנה could not be talking about that.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (trying out a possible answer)
Everyone agrees
Fewer than two

phrases.english: If we say a contestation of one person,
but didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
Everyone agrees
a contestation is no fewer than two people!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא עַרְעָר חַד, וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה's עוררין is one person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן rules that a contestation needs at least two people, so one person is not a real contestation

steps.title: Two contesters create a 'two against two' standoff
steps.stepSummary: If two people contest, they are matched by the two who confirm the signatures, so why trust one pair over the other?
steps.simpleTranslation: But rather, two contesters? Then it is two against two. Why rely on these? Rely on those!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option, two contesters, and shows it also doesn't work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people say the גט is forged, and two people confirm the signatures. That is a tie between equal witnesses. So the משנה's ruling, that ratifying the signatures settles it, would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Two against two: equal sets of witnesses contradicting each other
What did you see? (Why prefer this side?)

phrases.english: But rather, a contestation of two people?
Then they are two against two,
phrases.notes: Two say it's forged, and two others confirm the signatures.

phrases.english: what did you see that you rely on these,
rely on those instead!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא עַרְעָר תְּרֵי? תְּרֵי וּתְרֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting one contester, tests and rejects two contesters
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה's עוררין is two people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two contesters against two confirmers is a tie, so confirming the signatures could not settle the matter

steps.title: The contester is the husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the עַרְעָר in the משנה is the husband himself claiming the גט is forged.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a contestation by the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer to 'how many contesters?': it is the husband himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband is not a witness, so רבי יוחנן's two-person rule doesn't apply. His objection is still serious enough to require ratification. Once the signatures are confirmed, there is no tie, because his claim is not testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: A contestation raised by the husband

steps.whatToRemember: The 'contesters' in the משנה means the husband claiming forgery. That is why ratifying the signatures settles the matter.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a contestation by the husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 in a way that avoids both difficulties of steps 7 and 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עַרְעָר is the husband claiming the גט is forged

steps.title: New משנה: a גט from overseas without the declaration
steps.stepSummary: If the שליח bringing a גט from overseas cannot say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם', the גט can be ratified through the witnesses signed on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who brings a גט from overseas and cannot say 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence': if there are witnesses on it, it should be ratified through its signers.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives a backup way to validate a גט from overseas when the שליח cannot make the usual declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the שליח's declaration 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם' is what validates a גט from overseas. If he cannot say it, the גט is not lost. It can be validated like any regular document, by confirming the signatures of the witnesses on it.

keyTerms.meaning: A country overseas (outside ארץ ישראל)
'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence': the שליח's standard declaration
Witnesses (here, those signed on the גט)

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who brings a bill of divorce from a country overseas
and is unable to say
"It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence,"
if there are witnesses signed on it,
it should be ratified through its signers.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמֵּבִיא גֵּט מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם, וְאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לוֹמַר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט from overseas without the שליח's declaration can still be validated by ratifying the signatures of its witnesses

steps.title: Divorce documents and slave-freeing documents follow the same rules for delivery
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by saying that גיטי נשים and שחרורי עבדים follow the same rules for taking them overseas and bringing them back. It adds that this is one of several ways the two are alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bills of divorce and bills of freeing slaves are the same, whether someone takes them out of the land or brings them in. This is one of the ways the two kinds of documents are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its teaching by saying that a bill of freeing a slave works just like a גט for a woman when it travels to or from overseas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything said so far about a שליח bringing a גט also applies to a שליח bringing a document that frees a slave. This includes having to say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם. The words 'one of the ways' hint that the two documents are alike in other ways too, and the גמרא will list those ways soon.

keyTerms.meaning: Bills of divorce given to women
Documents that free a slave
One who takes a document out (from ארץ ישראל to overseas)
One who brings a document in (from overseas to ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: Both bills of divorce for women
and bills that free slaves
are the same for the one who takes them out and the one who brings them in,
phrases.notes: 'Takes out' means from ארץ ישראל to overseas; 'brings in' means from overseas to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: and this is one of the ways
in which bills of divorce are equal to bills that free slaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד גִּיטֵּי נָשִׁים וְאֶחָד שִׁחְרוּרֵי עֲבָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה that began with the שליח who cannot say בפני נכתב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rules for delivering a document to or from overseas apply equally to גיטי נשים and שחרורי עבדים.

steps.title: What does 'he cannot say' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins and asks what the משנה means when it speaks of a שליח who 'cannot say' בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does 'he is unable to say' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question about an earlier line of the משנה. It is setting up the challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה said that if the שליח 'cannot say' the required words, the גט can be confirmed through its signing witnesses. The גמרא wants to know what situation stops a valid שליח from speaking.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
He is unable to say

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the meaning of 'he is unable to say'?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה's case in step 10, where the שליח cannot say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's earlier line in step 10 to define what it is talking about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What situation leaves the שליח unable to make his statement?

steps.title: It cannot mean a deaf-mute, who may not be a שליח at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the שליח is a חרש, but rejects this. A משנה teaches that a חרש, a שוטה and a קטן may not bring a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he is a deaf-mute, can a deaf-mute bring a גט at all? But we learned: Anyone may bring a גט except a deaf-mute, a person who is not mentally competent, and a child!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the obvious answer, that the שליח is a deaf-mute, and immediately shows why that cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש is not considered mentally capable in הלכה, so he cannot serve as a שליח in the first place. The משנה cannot be giving a way to save a גט brought by someone who was never allowed to bring it. So the case must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, who in הלכה is treated as not legally capable
A person who is not mentally competent
A child who is not yet of age

phrases.english: If we say he is a deaf-mute,
is a deaf-mute someone who can bring a גט?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִין לְהָבִיא אֶת הַגֵּט,
phrases.english: But didn't we learn: Everyone is fit to bring a גט,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה found later in this מסכת, on דף כג.

phrases.english: except a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a child!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא חֵרֵשׁ חֵרֵשׁ בַּר אֵתוֹיֵי גִּיטָּא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one possible answer to the question in step 12 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה's 'cannot say' means a deaf-mute שליח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה teaches that a חרש can never bring a גט, so the משנה would not discuss saving a גט that he brought.

steps.title: רב יוסף: he became a deaf-mute after handing over the גט
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the שליח was fully capable when he gave the גט to the woman. He became a חרש before he managed to say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Here we are dealing with a case where he gave her the גט while he was fully capable, and before he managed to say 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence,' he became a deaf-mute.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge. The שליח was valid when he acted and lost the ability to speak only afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a valid שליח depends on his condition when he delivers the גט, and at that time he was a פיקח. He only lost the ability to make the required statement afterward. That is why the משנה needs another way to back up the גט: through the witnesses signed on it.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? (used to narrow the case)
A person who is fully capable (can hear and speak)
He became a deaf-mute

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where he gave it to her while he was fully capable,
and he did not manage to say
'It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence'
before he became a deaf-mute.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Cannot say' meant a שליח who was a deaf-mute from the start, which would make him unfit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שליח was capable when he delivered the גט and became a deaf-mute before making his statement.
steps.whatToRemember: A שליח who was fully capable when he delivered the גט stays a valid שליח. If he later loses the ability to speak, the גט can be confirmed through its witnesses instead.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא allows a חרש to be a שליח. He was a פיקח when he delivered the גט and only lost his speech afterward.

steps.title: A ברייתא: three ways the two documents are alike, starting with delivery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line and brings a ברייתא that lists three ways גיטי נשים and שחרורי עבדים are alike. The first way is the rule for taking them out and bringing them in.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Both bills of divorce and bills of freeing slaves': The Rabbis taught: In three ways bills of divorce are equal to bills of freeing slaves. They are equal for the one who takes them out and the one who brings them in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the end of the משנה. It brings a ברייתא that spells out what 'one of the ways' was hinting at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said this was 'one of the ways' the two documents are alike. The ברייתא names the full number, three. The first way is the same delivery rule the משנה just taught: the שליח must say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם, and his word is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה
Ways, ways in which two things are alike

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד גִּיטֵּי נָשִׁים וְאֶחָד שִׁיחְרוּרֵי עֲבָדִים:
phrases.english: 'Both bills of divorce and bills that free slaves':
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the last line of the משנה from step 11 before discussing it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: In three ways are equal
bills of divorce and bills that free slaves:
they are equal for the one who takes them out and the one who brings them in;

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּרָכִים שָׁווּ גִּיטֵּי נָשִׁים לְשִׁיחְרוּרֵי עֲבָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the end of the משנה from step 11 and brings a ברייתא to spell it out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three ways גיטי נשים and שחרורי עבדים are alike. The first is the rule for delivering them to or from overseas.

steps.title: Second way: a כותי witness is accepted on these two documents
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. A document with a כותי witness signed on it is normally invalid, but גיטי נשים and שחרורי עבדים are an exception. The text then begins the third way, about all documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: And any document that has a כותי witness signed on it is invalid, except bills of divorce and bills of freeing slaves. And all documents...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the second way the two documents are alike: a כותי witness is accepted on them. Then it starts the third way, which continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a כותי witness makes a document פסול. גיטי נשים and שחרורי עבדים are an exception to that rule, and are accepted with such a witness. The words 'and all documents' open the third rule, which is finished on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: A Samaritan witness
Invalid
Documents, legal papers

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל גֵּט שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו עֵד כּוּתִי – פָּסוּל,
phrases.english: And any document that has a Samaritan witness on it is invalid,
except for bills of divorce and bills that free slaves;
and all documents
phrases.notes: This sentence opens the third way, and it continues on the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל גֵּט שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו עֵד כּוּתִי פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list with its second item and starts the third.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כותי witness makes most documents invalid, but גיטי נשים and שחרורי עבדים are an exception and are accepted with one.
